zadanie: A 10-by-12-inch page has margins of 1.5 inches on all sides. What fraction of the area of the page is taken up by the margins? Express your answer as a common fraction.
oczekiwana_odpowiedz: A 10-by-12-inch paper will have an area of $10 \cdot 12 = 120$ square inches. If that paper has 1.5 inch margins on all sides, then the portion of the paper that is not covered by margins will be a rectangular section with length $12 - 2(1.5) = 9$ inches and width $10 - 2(1.5) = 7$ inches. Thus, $9 \cdot 7 = 63$ square inches of the paper will not be taken up by the margins. Since the paper has a total area of $120$ square in, this means that $120-63=57$ square inches of the page is taken up by margins. Thus, margins take up $\dfrac{57}{120}=\boxed{\dfrac{19}{40}}$ of the page.

[AI]:
To find the fraction of the area of the page taken up by the margins, we need to first calculate the area of the page and the area of the margins. 

The area of the page is the product of its length and width. 

The area of the margins can be found by subtracting the area of the inner rectangle (the area inside the margins) from the area of the page.

We will use the python_interpreter to perform these calculations and find the fraction of the area taken up by the margins.

```python
# define the dimensions of the page and margins
page_length = 12  # inches
page_width = 10  # inches
margin = 1.5  # inches

# calculate the area of the page
page_area = page_length * page_width

# calculate the dimensions of the inner rectangle
inner_length = page_length - 2 * margin
inner_width = page_width - 2 * margin

# calculate the area of the inner rectangle
inner_area = inner_length * inner_width

# calculate the area of the margins
margins_area = page_area - inner_area

# calculate the fraction of the area taken up by the margins
fraction = margins_area / page_area

print(fraction)
```
